questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Therapeutic Diet for Hypertension (DASH Diet) (Nutrition, Food Science and Technology)?

options.text: High saturated animal fats and refined table sugar with zero dietary fiber
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Selected a factually correct statement instead of identifying the exception.

options.text: High potassium, calcium, magnesium, and dietary fiber with restricted sodium intake
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the incorrect statement regarding Therapeutic Diet for Hypertension (DASH Diet).

options.text: High sodium chloride intake with complete restriction of green vegetables
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Failed to distinguish valid properties from the invalid exception.

options.text: Exclusive consumption of red processed meats without water
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Overlooked the 'NOT' constraint in the question stem.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
In Nutrition, Food Science and Technology (Therapeutic Diet for Hypertension (DASH Diet)):
The statement 'High potassium, calcium, magnesium, and dietary fiber with restricted sodium intake' is incorrect (and hence the correct answer to the exception question).
All other statements represent valid NCERT characteristics.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct choice.

questionText: [Set 30.2] In pediatric clinical assessment, Kwashiorkor is clinically distinguished from Marasmus by the prominent presence of:

options.text: Oedema (fluid accumulation in legs and face) and enlarged fatty liver with adequate calorie intake but acute protein deficiency
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Nutritional Deficiency: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus.

options.text: Severe muscle wasting and subcutaneous fat depletion without oedema (skin and bone appearance)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Vitamin C scurvy bleeding gums exclusively
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Excessive subcutaneous adipose tissue and childhood obesity
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Nutrition, Food Science and Technology (Nutritional Deficiency: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus):
Oedema (fluid accumulation in legs and face) and enlarged fatty liver with adequate calorie intake but acute protein deficiency

Detailed Context:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Public Nutrition and Health - Nutritional Deficiency: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus):
Kwashiorkor is caused by acute protein deficiency despite sufficient caloric intake, leading to generalized oedema, enlarged fatty liver, lethargy, and a 'moon face'. Marasmus is total protein-energy malnutrition characterized by severe wasting without oedema

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 46.3] In industrial dairy technology, High-Temperature Short-Time (HTST) pasteurization of milk involves heating milk to:

options.text: 100°C for two hours under boiling pressure
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: 63°C for fifteen seconds followed by storage at room temperature
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: 71.7°C (approx 72°C) for at least 15 seconds, followed by rapid cooling to below 4°C
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Pasteurization of Milk (HTST Method).

options.text: 140°C for twenty minutes continuously
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Pasteurization of Milk (HTST Method) (Nutrition, Food Science and Technology):
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Food Processing and Technology - Pasteurization of Milk (HTST Method)):
HTST pasteurization heats milk to $71.7^\circ\text{C}$ ($161^\circ\text{F}$) for 15 seconds, which destroys pathogenic vegetative microorganisms (e.g., Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Coxiella burnetii) without impairing milk flavor.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 30.9] The dietary approach recommended in clinical nutrition for managing hypertension (DASH diet) emphasizes:

options.text: High saturated animal fats and refined table sugar with zero dietary fiber
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: High sodium chloride intake with complete restriction of green vegetables
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: High potassium, calcium, magnesium, and dietary fiber with restricted sodium intake
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Therapeutic Diet for Hypertension (DASH Diet).

options.text: Exclusive consumption of red processed meats without water
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Nutrition, Food Science and Technology (Therapeutic Diet for Hypertension (DASH Diet)):
High potassium, calcium, magnesium, and dietary fiber with restricted sodium intake

Detailed Context:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Clinical Nutrition and Dietetics - Therapeutic Diet for Hypertension (DASH Diet)):
The DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, poultry, fish, and nuts, reducing sodium, red meats, sweets, and saturated fats to lower blood pressure.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
